description:

Location: Lincoln
Contract length: 6 months rolling contract (long-term potential)
Work Structure: Onsite

Randstad Sourceright, a leading provider of RPO & MSP Recruitment Services is currently recruiting for a Data Coordinator to join a World leader offering Products, Solutions and Services across the entire Energy value chain on behalf of a well established manufacturing organisation to play a key role in supporting Manufacturing Operations.

The Data Co-ordinator manages data and systems for early careers and apprenticeship programs. Responsibilities include running the Learner Management System (LMS), tracking Individual Learner Records (ILRs) to secure government funding, and keeping records compliant with Ofsted and ESFA standards. The role also handles apprentice registrations, partner college paperwork, and administrative support, requiring strong organizational skills, IT proficiency, and clear communication.

Some of the duties will include but are not limited to:
- Maintain and update the Learner Management System (LMS) with accurate student records.
- Send monthly data updates to service providers to ensure Individual Learner Records (ILRs) are correctly submitted.
- Ensure all data handling complies with official rules set by Ofsted, the Education Skills Funding Agency (ESFA), and awarding bodies.
- Design and generate reports to track government funding received through the Apprenticeship Levy.
- Stay up-to-date on government funding rules and requirements.
- Double-check data entries so the company receives all the funding it is eligible for.
- Act as the main point of contact for external LMS software providers to improve and update system features.
- Prepare and share essential onboarding documentation for colleges, external training providers, learners, and internal teams at the start of each academic year.
- Register new apprentices with official awarding organizations.
- Process and claim completion certificates once learners finish their programs.
- Review current office tools and workflows to find ways to make administrative tasks faster and more efficient.
- Provide general administrative support to the broader Skills & Education team as needed.

Essential Requirements:
- Excellent verbal and written communication abilities to liaise with external providers, colleges, and internal teams.
- Strong organizational skills to manage multiple learner records, meet strict funding deadlines, and handle varied tasks.
- A good working knowledge of IT systems, including experience with data management tools and software like Learner Management Systems (LMS).
- The ability to take initiative, solve problems, and work independently as part of a virtual team.
- Good presentation skills to clearly share funding reports, data trends, and process updates with the team.

Desirable Requirements:
- Prior experience working with Education Skills Funding Agency (ESFA) rules, funding methodologies, or managing the Apprenticeship Levy pool.
- Direct experience preparing, validating, or submitting Individual Learner Records (ILRs) using data compliance tools.
- Familiarity with popular apprenticeship and learner management software systems (such as Maytas, Aptem, OneFile, or Tribal).
- Prior experience participating in or preparing documentation for Ofsted inspections or external funding audits in a training/further education environment.
- Strong proficiency in advanced Excel functions (VLOOKUP, Pivot Tables) or data visualization tools (like Power BI) to generate detailed funding insights.

title: Payroll Specialist
description:
Payroll & Finance Administrator

Salary: £38,379 per annum
Location: Lincoln - 100% onsite
Contract: Permanent, full-time (37 hours per week)
Closing Date: ASAP / Ongoing - applications considered on a rolling basis

Marble Mayne Recruitment is delighted to be supporting a Students' Union in Lincoln with the recruitment of a Payroll & Finance Administrator. This is a newly created position offering an exciting opportunity for an experienced payroll professional to take ownership of a significant payroll improvement project, whilst also supporting the wider finance function.

The organisation employs approximately 70 permanent staff alongside a further 60 student and bar staff, creating a varied and relatively complex payroll environment.

Currently, payroll administration involves a combination of spreadsheets, timesheet systems and manual processes, with the University undertaking the final tax calculations. The organisation is now looking to bring its payroll operations fully in-house, with the ambition of developing a streamlined, automated, one-stop payroll solution by early to mid-2028.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys getting under the skin of existing processes, identifying improvements and implementing more efficient ways of working.

About the Role

Reporting to the Group Finance Manager, the role will be approximately 70% payroll focused and 30% broader finance administration.

Initially, you will need to develop a thorough understanding of how payroll currently operates across the organisation, taking ownership of existing processes whilst reviewing opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency and automation.

Working closely with senior finance and HR colleagues, you will play a central role in designing and implementing a new integrated payroll solution, reducing manual intervention and ultimately bringing the entire payroll process together.

Alongside this project, you will be responsible for ensuring accurate and timely payroll administration, including timesheet management, payroll calculations, statutory deductions, pensions, reconciliations and compliance with relevant legislation.

The remaining 30% of the role will involve supporting the wider finance team with purchase and sales ledger processing, expenses, reconciliations, month-end activities and general financial administration.

About You

We are looking for someone with strong, hands-on, end-to-end payroll experience who is comfortable working in a varied and potentially complex payroll environment.

Ideally, you will have worked within a small/medium sized organisation where you have needed to take responsibility for multiple aspects of payroll, rather than specialising in one narrow area within a large payroll department.

Experience within hospitality, commercial organisations, charities or similarly varied environments would be particularly relevant.

You will need to demonstrate experience of managing payroll for a mixture of permanent salaried employees and weekly paid, casual or variable-hours staff, including dealing with different pay rates, timesheets and working patterns.

Strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation, statutory deductions, pensions and payroll systems is essential, alongside excellent Excel skills.

Importantly, we are also looking for someone who enjoys improving processes and systems. Previous experience of implementing payroll improvements, introducing automation or supporting a payroll systems transition would be particularly valuable.

As this is a combined payroll and finance position, you will also need some practical finance or accounting experience, ideally including transaction processing, reconciliations and working with accounting systems.

You will be organised, accurate, proactive and confident working independently, with the communication skills to engage effectively with colleagues across the organisation.

Location and Working Arrangements

Please note that this is a 100% onsite position based in Lincoln, with no hybrid or remote working arrangements available. Due to the operational nature of the role, the need to work closely with colleagues and the significant payroll transformation project ahead, the successful candidate will be required to work onsite five days per week.

Application Process

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with no fixed closing date. Early applications are therefore encouraged.

title: Supply Chain Coordinator
description:
When materials arrive on time, stock levels are right and production runs without delays, it's because someone has kept everything moving behind the scenes. As a Supply Chain Coordinator, you'll be the person making that happen, keeping suppliers, deliveries and internal teams working together to avoid disruption and keep operations running smoothly.
You'll join a growing organisation where your ability to plan ahead, solve problems and keep things organised will make a real difference. From managing purchase orders to improving supplier performance, you'll have the opportunity to influence how efficiently the business operates.
What's in it for you?
- Salary of 27,000 - 29,000 per annum.
- Permanent position offering long-term stability within a growing organisation.
- Company pension scheme and holiday allowance.
- Training and development opportunities to build your skills.
- Employee assistance programme to support your wellbeing.
- Career progression opportunities as the business continues to grow.

Your responsibilities as Supply Chain Coordinator
- Raise and track purchase orders, ensuring materials arrive on time to meet production requirements.
- Monitor stock levels, support inventory planning and help prevent shortages or unnecessary delays.
- Liaise with suppliers on pricing, lead times and deliveries, resolving issues before they affect operations.
- Work closely with warehouse, production and logistics teams to keep goods moving efficiently.
- Maintain accurate records, monitor supplier performance and produce reports on stock availability and delivery performance.
- Support demand forecasting and identify opportunities to reduce costs, improve processes and strengthen service levels.

- Previous experience in supply chain, logistics, procurement or inventory management.
